title: Interactive Water Surface with Ripples
prompt:
Create a single HTML file that implements an interactive 3D water surface simulation with ripple physics, floating objects, and reflective shading using Three.js.

## Three.js Import (MUST follow exactly)
In the <head>, use this importmap and import via ES Module in <script type="module">:
```html
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';
</script>
```

## Scene Setup
- Background color: 0x87CEEB (sky blue). Add a large sky-colored hemisphere or gradient.
- PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 8, 12), looking at (0, 0, 0).
- OrbitControls enabled.
- DirectionalLight at (5, 10, 5) intensity 1.0, casting shadows. AmbientLight intensity 0.3.
- Environment: create a simple skybox effect by using scene.background set to a light blue color and adding fog (THREE.FogExp2, color 0x87CEEB, density 0.015).

## Water Surface (Height-Field Simulation)
- Create a PlaneGeometry grid of size 20x20 with resolution 128x128 segments (129x129 vertices). Orient it horizontally (rotate -PI/2 around x-axis) at y=0.
- Maintain two height arrays: h_current[i][j] and h_previous[i][j], each of size 129x129, initialized to 0.
- Each frame, apply the 2D wave equation:
  h_new[i][j] = 2 * h_current[i][j] - h_previous[i][j] + c^2 * dt^2 * laplacian(h_current, i, j) - damping * (h_current[i][j] - h_previous[i][j])
  where laplacian = (h[i+1][j] + h[i-1][j] + h[i][j+1] + h[i][j-1] - 4*h[i][j]) / (dx^2)
  c = wave speed (adjustable, default 8.0), dt = 1/60, dx = 20/128, damping = 0.02 (adjustable).
- After computing h_new, shift: h_previous = h_current, h_current = h_new.
- Update the PlaneGeometry vertex y-positions from h_current. Call geometry.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true and geometry.computeVertexNormals() each frame.

## Water Material
- Use MeshPhongMaterial or MeshStandardMaterial with:
  - color: 0x006994 (dark teal blue)
  - transparent: true, opacity: 0.8
  - Load water_normals.jpg as a normal map from './water_normals.jpg'. Set normalScale to (0.5, 0.5).
  - shininess: 100 (if Phong) or metalness: 0.1, roughness: 0.2 (if Standard).
  - side: THREE.DoubleSide.
- The normal map provides fine detail on top of the simulation-driven vertex displacement.

## Click-to-Ripple Interaction
- When the user clicks on the water surface, use raycasting to find the intersection point.
- At the intersection grid cell (i, j), create a ripple by setting h_current[i][j] = -rippleStrength (default 1.5) in a small circular area (radius ~3 cells).
- The ripple should propagate outward according to the wave equation.
- Slider id='slider-ripple' controls ripple strength (range 0.5-5.0, step 0.1, default 1.5, label 'Ripple Strength').

## Floating Duck (Duck.glb)
- Load Duck.glb from './Duck.glb'. Scale to approximately 0.5 units.
- Position the duck on the water surface. Each frame, sample the water height at the duck's (x, z) position and set the duck's y to that height + a small offset (so it sits on the surface).
- The duck should also tilt (rotate around x and z) based on the local water surface gradient at its position, simulating buoyancy alignment.
- The duck drifts slowly in a random direction (speed 0.3 m/s). When it reaches the edge (|x| > 9 or |z| > 9), reverse direction.
- Button id='btn-add-duck' adds another Duck.glb clone (max 5 ducks total). Each new duck starts at a random position.

## Automatic Rain Mode
- Button id='btn-rain' toggles rain mode. In rain mode, every 200ms a random ripple is created at a random position on the water surface with strength 0.5.
- Rain creates many small ripples, producing a natural rainfall effect.

## Controls
- Slider id='slider-ripple': range 0.5-5.0, step 0.1, default 1.5. Ripple strength on click.
- Slider id='slider-wavespeed': range 2.0-15.0, step 0.5, default 8.0. Wave propagation speed c.
- Slider id='slider-damping': range 0.005-0.1, step 0.005, default 0.02. Wave damping factor.
- Button id='btn-add-duck': Add a floating duck (max 5).
- Button id='btn-rain': Toggle rain mode.
- Button id='btn-reset': Reset water surface to flat, remove extra ducks, stop rain.
- Keyboard: 'p' toggles pause, 'r' toggles rain.

## HUD (id='hud')
- Position: top-left, semi-transparent dark background, padding 12px, monospace 14px, white text.
- Sub-elements:
  - id='hud-maxheight': current maximum water height across the grid.
  - id='hud-ducks': number of ducks on the water.
  - id='hud-rain': 'ON' or 'OFF' rain mode.
  - id='hud-wavespeed': current wave speed value.
  - id='hud-damping': current damping value.
  - id='hud-ripples': total number of ripples created since start.

## State Management
Every frame, update window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- frameCount (int): incremented each frame.
- maxWaterHeight (float): maximum absolute height value across all grid vertices.
- minWaterHeight (float): minimum height value.
- avgWaterHeight (float): average height value.
- duckCount (int): number of ducks on the water.
- duckPositions (array): each { x, y, z } of duck world positions.
- waveSpeed (float): current wave speed c.
- dampingFactor (float): current damping.
- rippleStrength (float): current ripple strength setting.
- totalRipples (int): total number of ripples created.
- rainMode (boolean): whether rain mode is active.
- waterValid (boolean): true if maxWaterHeight is finite and < 10 (no explosion), duckCount >= 1.
- isPaused (boolean): pause state.
physics_constraints: 2D wave equation: h_new = 2*h - h_old + c^2*dt^2*(laplacian) - damping*(h - h_old). Laplacian uses 4-neighbor finite differences. Boundary condition: fixed edges at h=0. Energy should dissipate over time due to damping > 0. Wave speed c controls propagation rate. Duck buoyancy: y_duck = h_water(x_duck, z_duck) + offset. Duck tilt from surface gradient: dh/dx and dh/dz at duck position.
